paragraphs: In Sotah 30a he speaks in the name of Rav. Perhaps he is [Rabbah bar Itai, who lived in Rav’s time, as explained in the entry Rava bar Itai. In Sotah 30a, too, the reading should be “Rabbah bar Itai said in the name of Rabbah.” This requires further investigation.]

notes.text: The square-bracketed continuation is already part of the supplied source. Hyman ends with “this requires further investigation”; the Isi/Itai and Rav/Rabbah readings remain unresolved rather than merged.

Hyman’s tentative identification, supplied square brackets, Rabbah/Rava distinction, proposed אמר רבה wording and final requires further investigation remain intact. No new Sotah30a or DikdukeiSoferim apparatus was inspected. Neither the conjectured name nor its transmission chain is treated as a newly proved identity or textual correction.

Hyman’s printed notice breaks off after “perhaps he is.” The supplied brackets enclose the continuation from the following heading. Davidson’s Sotah 30a has Rav Asi transmitting in Rav’s name, with Rabbah ben Isi as the alternate transmitter. Bomberg instead reads Rav Ashi in the first attribution. Munich 95 gives Rabbah bar Isi in both versions, first in Rav’s name and then in Rav Yosef’s. Hyman’s suggested “Rabbah bar Itai in Rabbah’s name” remains conjectural.
